theme_central: Short but extremely dense: the code of good manners (akhlaq) that founds a harmonious society — from verifying information to the affirmation that only piety confers nobility.
sources_note: Well-sourced structure (alim.org, thelastdialogue.org): 1-5, 6-9, then social ethics and brotherhood widely documented.

branches.title: Manners toward Allah and the Prophet
branches.resume: Not to precede Allah and His messenger, to lower one's voice; hence the surah's name, those who call out from behind the private chambers (hujurat).

children.t: Not to precede Allah and His messenger, lowering one's voice in his presence
Those who call out from behind the private chambers lack reason

branches.title: Verifying information
branches.resume: If a corrupt person brings news, verify before acting so as not to harm a people out of ignorance.

children.t: Verifying information before acting, not harming out of ignorance

branches.title: Reconciliation, brotherhood
branches.resume: Reconciling two groups of believers in conflict; the believers are brothers.

children.t: Reconciliation between believers in conflict, brotherhood of faith

branches.title: Mockery, slander, true nobility
branches.resume: Not to mock, not to slander; mankind created diverse in order to know one another; only piety confers nobility.

children.t: Not to mock, not to insult one another, avoiding suspicion and backbiting
Diversity of peoples in order to know one another; only piety confers nobility

branches.title: True faith vs verbal declaration
branches.resume: The desert Arabs say they believe but faith has not yet entered their hearts; true believers defined, closing.

children.t: True faith of the true believers, distinct from mere verbal declaration
